item.title: Carney agrees 'in principle' to Trump's Gaza peace board; details to be worked out
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters Sunday he has agreed in principle to join U.S. President Donald Trump's controversial "Board of Peace," meant to support the reconstruction of Gaza.

item.title: Carney 'concerned' about U.S. 'escalation' on Greenland after tariffs
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he is "concerned" about U.S. "escalation" on its push to buy Greenland after it threatened to impose tariffs on eight European nations opposed to the U.S. plan for the self-governing Danish territory.

item.title: Lack of snow prompts Mount Washington to adapt with events and challenges
item.description: A stretch of unseasonably warm weather is leaving Mount Washington Alpine Resort with little fresh snow, but the Vancouver Island ski hill is finding ways to keep the season lively despite the dry spell.

item.title: Researchers capture rare glimpse of transient killer whales hunting sea lion off Victoria
item.description: A rare and dramatic encounter with transient killer whales has been documented off the coast of Victoria, offering a glimpse into the hunting behaviour of one of the ocean's top predators.

item.title: Four UVic student athletes recognized by Greater Victoria Sports Hall of Fame
item.description: Four first-year University of Victoria student athletes are being recognized by the Greater Victoria Sports Hall of Fame for their excellence in athletics, academics, and community leadership.

item.title: BC Hydro surpasses 800 public fast charging ports across B.C.
item.description: BC Hydro says it has surpassed a key milestone in expanding B.C.’s electric vehicle charging network, now operating more than 800 public fast-charging ports provincewide as EV demand continues to grow.

item.title: B.C. and ʼNa̱mǥis First Nation advance Gw'ani land-use plan for Nimpkish Valley
item.description: The B.C. government and the 'Na̱mg̱is First Nation have taken another step toward reshaping land-use planning in the Nimpkish Valley.

item.title: Conservative MLA Sheldon Clare says leadership rules meant to stop 'funny business'
item.description: A leadership candidate for British Columbia's Conservatives says recently announced rules for the contest are intended to stop "any funny business" following last year's leadership review that was marred by fraud allegations.

item.title: Fire crews save house after explosion, fire in West Kelowna
item.description: Firefighters in West Kelowna, B.C., say they managed to save a house from flames early Sunday morning following reports of an explosion.

item.title: Dense fog warning persists near Port Alberni as near-zero visibility lingers
item.description: A yellow fog warning remains in effect for inland Vancouver Island near Port Alberni, with near-zero visibility expected to continue through Tuesday afternoon, according to Environment Canada.
